cohort: The study included 80 pregnant women undergoing elective or emergency cesarean delivery at a tertiary care teaching hospital.
finding: Intraoperative vaginal preparation tended to reduce surgical site infections (though not statistically significant), and spinal anesthesia was associated with a significantly lower surgical site infection incidence compared to general anesthesia.
mod_finding: Intraoperative vaginal preparation and spinal anesthesia during cesarean sections were found to be associated with lower rates of surgical site infections, suggesting preferred practices for this mode of birth.
